prompt: A debugging session investigated why the hot-reload path silently skips files with certain unicode filenames. The validator downstream still runs but operates on stale state. Three hypotheses were tested; the third (encoding normalisation in the watcher) was confirmed. The fix is one line but needs regression coverage for non-ASCII paths. Compress this into an ops-ready handoff note under 60 words.

Three engineers spent two hours debugging a websocket reconnect loop. Root cause: the exponential backoff timer resets on every auth token refresh, which fires every 55 seconds — shorter than max backoff. The heartbeat check masks the symptom by keeping the connection alive. Real fix requires coordinating the backoff ceiling with the token TTL. Compress into a one-paragraph incident summary.

Post-mortem: duplicate job scheduling caused by a race between the scheduler acquiring a distributed lock and the lock-TTL expiring during high-latency DB reads. Jobs with execution time > lock TTL were at risk. The fix adds a lock-renewal heartbeat. The idempotency key layer prevents duplicate side-effects but does not prevent duplicate executions. Compress to three bullet points for the incident channel.

A token refresh race was found where two concurrent requests could both hit the refresh endpoint within the same validity window and each receive valid tokens, resulting in one being silently dropped. The auth surface is not to be widened. The preferred fix is a per-user mutex on the refresh path, but this requires Redis. The fallback is idempotent refresh with a dedup window. Compress to an engineering decision brief.

A cache invalidation bug: mutation writes update the primary store but the read cache checks a stale version key rather than the entity key. Hot-path read latency must stay under 20ms so a full-scan invalidation strategy is ruled out. The fix is targeted: update the version key on every write. Two edge cases remain open — bulk mutations and TTL-expired reads returning before write propagates. Compress to a patch brief.

Plugin load order is nondeterministic across restarts because plugins self-register via an import side-effect and Python import order varies with PYTHONPATH and module cache state. Extension compatibility must not be broken. The fix is an explicit load-order manifest file. It requires migrating existing implicit registrations, which will be a breaking change for plugins that depended on ordering accidents. Compress to a migration-notice draft.

CLI override precedence is broken: flags passed on the command line are overridden by values loaded from config files because the merge order reads config last. Default fallback values must still work. The fix inverts the merge order but requires careful testing on cases where config is intentionally authoritative. Affected users: anyone using both --flag overrides and a config file. Compress to a release-note entry.

A partial sync corruption was found: when an upload is interrupted mid-stream, the checksum recorded in the manifest reflects the partial file, not the intended full file. On resumption, the system considers the upload complete. Checksum verification must be preserved. The fix requires writing a pending-checksum field that is promoted to final only on successful close. Schema migration required. Compress to a data-integrity incident brief.

Session reuse is causing connection pool exhaustion: sessions are marked reusable before teardown is complete, so a new request acquires a session that is still mid-close. The connection explosion risk arises when teardown is slow under load. The fix adds a CLOSING state between ACTIVE and REUSABLE. The CLOSING → REUSABLE transition is guarded by a completion callback. Compress to a state-machine change note.

Settings mismatch between UI state and persistence: the UI optimistically applies changes and the persistence layer writes asynchronously. On slow connections, the user can trigger a second change before the first write completes, and the second write arrives first. The result is a persistent state that does not match the last user intent. The fix is a write queue with per-setting serialisation. Compress to a product-bug summary for the support team.
